channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Microsoft’s MAI Code 2 claims 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the price — and developers are pushing back
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Microsoft unveiled seven in-house MAI models at Ignite, led by a coding model it says nearly matches Claude Opus 5.5 for a twentieth of the cost. The catch, buried in the fine print and all over Reddit: the price is promotional, the tests are Microsoft’s own, and the developers it needs to convince aren’t convinced yet.

item.title: Turn a technical book into a Claude Code skill: hands-on with book-to-skill
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: book-to-skill turns any technical book into a structured agent skill — frameworks, decision rules, and anti-patterns your coding agent loads on demand. This tutorial installs it, extracts a real book and a real PDF, and generates a working skill, with every command verified.

item.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: cheaper, faster — and its first model rated High for AI self-improvement
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on November 17, with higher benchmark scores at lower prices — and Astra is the company’s first model rated High for AI self-improvement.

item.title: Ship a support agent on your own site: ChatKit and the OpenAI Agents SDK
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Agent Builder shuts down November 30, 2026. The replacement is a stack you own: ChatKit for the chat UI, the Agents SDK for the brain, and a Python server you run yourself — tools, guardrails, and all.

item.title: Design in your coding agent: hands-on with Google's Stitch skills
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google's Stitch skills put a UI design studio inside Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex: 16 skills, three plugins, and one MCP server between a text prompt and reviewed React components. This tutorial installs them, connects the MCP server, and runs the full loop — every command verified.

item.title: Corma hits a $1 billion valuation three months out of stealth — the bet that AI defense needs its own models
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Corma raised $125 million at a $1 billion valuation three months after leaving stealth, betting that cybersecurity defense deserves its own foundation models — not repurposed general-purpose ones.

item.title: Turn lab notes into a submission-ready paper: hands-on with Google Research's PaperOrchestra
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google Research's PaperOrchestra turns an idea and an experimental log into a submission-ready LaTeX manuscript with five specialised agents. It gained 1,175 stars in a day — this tutorial installs it, feeds it real materials, and shows exactly where the free tier ends.

item.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen gets hands: Google's Antigravity robotics plugin turns plain conversation into robot control
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google DeepMind posted a 31-second clip of a robot arm working from plain-English instructions — and launched a Robotics plugin that turns Antigravity into a workbench for going from simulation to hardware in about an hour.

item.title: Microsoft launches the AI Transparency Initiative: 40+ companies to set open standards for governing AI agents
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Microsoft unveiled the AI Transparency Initiative at Ignite, a joint effort with more than 40 companies to build open standards so enterprises can see what their AI agents do, verify it independently, and stay in control when models change.

item.title: Run MBZUAI's K2 Horizon on your own machine: the fully-open fleet from 0.9B to 375B
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: MBZUAI's K2 Horizon is a fully open fleet of six reasoning models, from 0.9B to 375B parameters — weights, training data, code, and checkpoints included. Run the 0.9B on a laptop CPU in ten minutes, then scale to the 375B flagship with the same API.

item.title: Perplexity crosses a $1 billion revenue run rate — and pulls its IPO forward to early 2027
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Perplexity has crossed a $1 billion annual revenue run rate, CEO Aravind Srinivas said onstage at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event — up from under $250 million in January. The company says it got there burning a fifth of Anthropic’s cash, and it may now file for an IPO as early as the first quarter of 2027.

item.title: Turn Claude Code into a bug bounty hunter: hands-on with Claude-BugHunter
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Claude-BugHunter is the number-one trending repo on GitHub: 83 Claude Code skills that turn a coding agent into a methodical bug bounty hunter. Install it, run a practice hunt on Juice Shop, and put your first finding through the 7-question validation gate — every deterministic step verified.

item.title: Higgsfield hands-on: Soul ID keeps one face consistent from photo to cinematic video
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Train a Soul ID from 20–80 photos for 25 credits, generate the portrait in Soul 2.0, then animate it in Cinema Studio with a real camera move — the same face, every scene.

item.title: Talk to Blender: build 3D scenes with Claude and MCP for Blender
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: MCP for Blender wires your LLM into Blender over a local socket: install the server, point your coding agent at it, and describe the scene you want. Every command below was run and verified — including a real render.

item.title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion to push AI-designed drugs toward human trials
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Isomorphic Labs has closed a $5 billion Series C co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, just six months after its $2.1 billion Series B. The money funds its IsoDDE drug-design engine and the push to take its first AI-designed medicines into human trials — the test the whole field has been waiting for.

item.title: Train your own LLM from scratch: hands-on with MiniMind's 64M-parameter model
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: MiniMind trains a 64-million-parameter language model from scratch for about ¥3 of GPU rental. This tutorial runs the whole pipeline — inference, a tiny pretraining pass, and SFT — on an ordinary CPU, with every command verified.

item.title: Nvidia’s Vera Rubin sweeps every MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark — but the headline 10x agentic gain is still provisional
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Nvidia’s Vera Rubin platform made its MLPerf debut on November 16, topping every Training v6.1 benchmark and posting up to twice the per-GPU performance of the GB300 systems it succeeds — while its eye-catching 10x agentic throughput-per-watt figure still awaits MLCommons verification.

item.title: Run the new open-weight speech champion yourself: hands-on with Salesforce's SOV-Transcribe-1
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Salesforce's SOV-Transcribe-1 leads every downloadable transcriber on the Artificial Analysis benchmark at 2.28% word error — and it takes plain-language instructions for how the transcript should read. This tutorial runs it two ways: a one-shot Transformers script and a vLLM server with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

item.title: Turn your coding agent into a film crew: hands-on with OpenFilm, the open-source AI video agent
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenFilm turns your coding agent into a film crew: a film is an HTML file, each shot a web page with one function, frame(t), and a real editor lets you change anything. We installed 0.3.2, wrote a four-second film by hand, and rendered a real 1920×1080 MP4 — no account, no API key, no video model.

item.title: DeepSeek starts rationing its free chatbot: daily quotas, 40,000-character prompts, and a compute shortage it can't hide
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: On November 16, DeepSeek's free app and web chat began capping single prompts at about 40,000 characters, dropping week-old conversations, and cutting users off with a daily quota — citing “insufficient computing power” — while its API stays pay-as-you-go.

item.title: Google: AI agents now turn security patches into working exploits with no human in the loop — and a North Korea-linked crew rigged Claude Code
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google’s threat intelligence team says attackers have crossed a line it had not seen before: AI agent frameworks that read a security patch, write the exploit and fire it, with no human in the loop. The same report describes a suspected North Korean crew turning Claude Code itself into a backdoor delivery pipe.

item.title: Build a fully local RAG app with LlamaIndex and llama.cpp — no API keys, no cloud
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: LlamaIndex 0.14.26 turns your own documents into a question-answering app in about 30 lines — with a local Qwen3 model and nomic embeddings, no API key, no GPU, $0. We ran it end to end on a CPU-only machine: 3/3 answers right, 4/5 top-1 retrievals, and a chat engine that remembers what 'they' means.

item.title: China's top AI labs are shipping new models with the hacking skills cut out
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Moonshot, Tencent and Alibaba have all shipped recent models with offensive cyber capabilities deliberately trimmed, Bloomberg reports — and Zhipu plans to gate its most sensitive functions behind verification. The shift follows Beijing's proposed export ban on offensive cyber AI.

item.title: Ditch headless Chrome: scrape, screenshot, and automate the web with Obscura's 70 MB Rust browser
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Obscura is a headless browser engine in Rust — no Chromium, a ~77 MB binary, ~35 MB of RAM — that fetches, renders, screenshots, and scrapes pages from the CLI, speaks CDP to Puppeteer and Playwright, and exposes 38 MCP tools to coding agents. Version 0.2.7, 36,014 stars, verified end to end.

item.title: OpenAI embeds four outside safety labs to test whether its models subvert their own rules
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI has signed four independent safety labs to work inside the company, testing whether its models try to work around their own safeguards — but the auditors say the access falls short of what real independence requires.
